issue.title: HOST-007: bounded interactive Normal/analog byte device emulator
issue.body:
## Scope and exact dependencies

Dot B HOST-007: a small deterministic interactive byte-level device peer for the existing Normal/analog host controller. Base HOST-006: `477057aadc9bc8e757bc8ef817125377e816d212` (PR #31; independent bounded PASS 10.0). This task creates new host-only files; it does not change session.py, wire.py, window.py, GUI, recordings, firmware, shared protocol, CI or merge policy.

Shared source is explicitly pinned to unaccepted PR #14 `c54bd955aaf3cb863ef3df043ea237ea62e74ad4`. HOST-006 retains its own b6ae pin; normal/analog compatibility must be tested rather than silently repinning it. This emulator is not firmware or hardware validation. Primary Critic-B's native TX queue evidence does not prove capture/dispatcher/physical USB.

## Ownership

Implementation worker: `host/motortester/device_emulator.py`, `host/tests/test_device_emulator.py`, `host/docs/device-emulator.md`.
Independent conformance worker: `host/tests/test_device_emulator_conformance.py`, `host/tests/fixtures/device_emulator/**`.
Two new internal Astra/xhigh workers, disjoint files, no git/index/branch/publication permissions. Root publishes the frozen result. User-facing documentation/messages are Russian; engineering coordination is English.

## Minimal API and bounds

Agree immutable results before coding. Proposed `DeviceEmulator.write(bytes, now_ms)` returns accepted prefix length plus bounded diagnostics; `read(max_bytes, now_ms)` returns output bytes accepted by the simulated transport; `trigger(now_ms)`, `tick(now_ms)`, `disconnect(now_ms)`, immutable `snapshot()`.
First returned frame byte commits its sequence; first END byte commits that terminal outcome. Last STOP_ACK byte clears the drain barrier. read(0) commits neither. Unaccepted write suffix remains caller-owned and must not be silently dropped.
Maximum 4096 input/output bytes per call, existing bounded RX accumulator, one current TX frame, at most eight control/status descriptors, one raw 4096-byte sample buffer, last RX replay and one terminal/tombstone. Generate DATA lazily; stop accepting input before mandatory-response capacity is exhausted. No unbounded histories/queues. Invalid Python types, oversize calls or nonmonotonic/out-of-range uint64 timestamps fail before mutation/copies.

## Supported behavior

Advertise only profile 1, Normal, analog, rising/falling, pretrigger 0. HELLO/GET_CAPS/CONFIG/ARM/STOP/GET_STATUS plus mandatory RELEASE_WINDOW are handled with exact pinned payloads, direction/session/sequence/request guards and error codes. Unsupported configuration is not advertised. No Auto/Single/external acquisition or firmware-copying.
Explicit synthetic trigger generates deterministic integer ADC codes, truthful trigger index/rail flags and sample CRC. Out-of-band immutable provenance says simulator, shared draft SHA, nominal timing and synthetic waveform; do not invent a wire provenance field or claim physical threshold/ADC evidence.
Include bounded RELEASE lifecycle: matching generation/window/CRC frees held buffer; rearm only after RELEASE_ACK completes; a late or repeated matching RELEASE with a new request ID gets ACK without a second rearm, including after Stop. Latest completed-window tombstone replaces prior one; older/mismatched RELEASE yields BAD_WINDOW_RELEASE. Stop/HELLO cancel continuation without a second terminal outcome.

## Explicit provisional hold-timeout assumption

A has not yet replied to [the clarification request](https://github.com/font-weight/stm32_motortester/pull/14#issuecomment-6097915092), verified before issue creation. Candidate interpretation: 5000 ms begins after the last END byte is accepted by simulated transport; elapsed >=5000 enters ERROR with STATUS.reason TRANSFER_TIMEOUT, preserves committed END/tombstone and never emits another ABORT/END. Label this exact assumption in public results/provenance/tests as PROVISIONAL until A confirms/corrects it in its source. It must not be reported as accepted wire semantics. This does not block independent framing/command/Stop implementation.

## Predeclared acceptance

1. Independent golden binary command/reply vectors and source SHA evidence; fragmented/coalesced commands, byte-at-a-time drains and no sequence consumption on read(0).
2. Twenty HOST-006 controller ARM -> trigger -> real BEGIN/DATA/END bytes -> STOP cycles; independent reconstruction validates exact 2048 samples/4096 bytes and CRC. END admission is not sample-validation success.
3. Raw-peer RELEASE cases: correct IDs/CRC, duplicate/new request IDs, wrong and older tombstones, rearm only after complete ACK, late RELEASE after Stop with no rearm, continuation and replacement by a later completed window.
4. Stop before BEGIN, mid-BEGIN/DATA, before first END byte, after first END byte, after full END, and around RELEASE_ACK. Preserve mandatory prior replies; exactly one terminal; no phantom/double ABORT, sequence gaps or old-generation data after STOP_ACK.
5. Fresh HELLO while old output frame is partial completes the started old frame before new ACK, resets new-session state, and never allows an old completion callback to mutate the new session.
6. Malformed framing/CRC/payload, wrong direction/session, replay/conflict/gaps, unknown types, boundaries/counter exhaustion, strict Python input/clock behavior, bounded queue/backpressure and retained-memory regression. No invented wire ERROR for undecodable input.
7. Hold deadline just-before/exact/after and Stop/RELEASE races run under the explicitly provisional interpretation; report these separately.
8. Author + independent focused suites, the entire new test set under Python -O (no setup side effects in bare asserts), full host suite with zero skips using existing offscreen GUI dependencies. Freeze source hashes before/after, preserve failed evidence honestly, publish exact manifest.
9. Independent Critic-B must review the exact published SHA against this scope and score >=9.5 before bounded acceptance. Shared-contract acceptance, Windows, physical transport, device timing and release readiness remain separate.

No implementation or publication claim is made by opening this issue.
